clue.text: See 22 down
Conservative potentate up for perjury, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the ruler's title is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an emir is a Muslim ruler, a potentate

explanation.surface: A Tory grandee climbs the ladder by lying under oath.
explanation.definitionFit: Perjury, lying under oath, is one example of an offence against the law, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Tory author

definitions.meaning: George ..., Conservative Chancellor of the Exchequer when the puzzle appeared
John ..., playwright of Look Back in Anger

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician who also writes books.
explanation.walkthrough: George Osborne was the Conservative Chancellor in 2014; John Osborne was the playwright behind Look Back in Anger. The theme author, Jeffrey Archer, was himself a Tory writer.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to a Conservative chancellor and to a celebrated English playwright.

clue.text: 24's e-book?

parts.note: a novel by the 24-across author, read cryptically: the letter e heads the word for peers, so its title describes where e stands

explanation.surface: Asks for an electronic book by the author at 24.
explanation.walkthrough: The e of 'e-book' is the opening letter of the last word of this Archer title, so the title describes the letter e's position in that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeffrey Archer wrote this 1984 political novel, and the title literally describes the letter e within its last word.

clue.text: I ask to safeguard leaders in expedition, frozen in glacial collapse

indicators.note: safeguarding means holding protectively, so the word for ask wraps round the leaders

parts.note: to call for something is to ask for it

indicators.note: the leaders of a phrase are the first letters of its words

explanation.surface: A climber asks for the expedition heads to be protected when caught up in an avalanche of ice.
explanation.definitionFit: An icefall is a steep, broken part of a glacier where ice tumbles down, a glacial collapse.

clue.text: Some egoist, even so, notorious author

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A writer described as a notorious egoist, for all that.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson, writer of Treasure Island, is a famous Scottish novelist.

clue.text: Bird magazine

definitions.meaning: bird is slang for a prison sentence, as in doing bird
the American news weekly of that name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is rhyming slang (bird-lime = time) for a jail term, apt in a puzzle about Jeffrey Archer, who served one.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing bird means serving a sentence, and the news weekly shares the word for that span.

clue.text: Difficult problem for gangster

definitions.meaning: a hard nut to crack, a tricky puzzle
a hard man, a thug or tough guy

explanation.surface: A knotty puzzle set for a mobster.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal word covers both a hard puzzle and a hard, violent man.

clue.text: Drink uses fish

parts.note: to milk something is to exploit or use it
hake is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A beverage that makes use of fish, a grim recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A milkshake is a sweet blended drink of milk and flavouring.

clue.text: Robin redbreast's opening wings to accelerate, furiously flying

indicators.note: furiously suggests wild agitation, so the gathered letters are thrown into a new order
the opening of a word is its first letter
the wings of a word are its two outer letters

explanation.surface: A robin opens its wings and speeds off in a frantic flutter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' takes R from redbreast's and 'wings' takes AE from accelerate; with ROBIN, 'furiously' rearranges the eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something airborne is up in the air, in flight.

clue.text: See 3
Old publisher picks up on leader in Times

parts.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A veteran newspaperman notices something about an editorial in The Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link: the letter from Times sits after the word for picks up.
explanation.definitionFit: William Randolph Hearst was the American newspaper magnate of the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Stone after May, the new birthstone for February

indicators.note: after places the stone abbreviation following the shuffled letters
new tells us the two words are made over into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: Talk of a gem that follows May, the latest birthstone chosen for February.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' reworks MAY and THE into AMETHY. ST is the stone, the British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The purple quartz gem is traditionally assigned to people born in February.

clue.text: Flower power, hugging resistance

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping round, so the power word encloses the resistance symbol

parts.note: steam is a source of power, as in steam engines
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Flower power clasping a protest movement, a sixties picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is read as something that flows, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A river or brook is a flower in the crossword sense: a thing that flows.

clue.text: Whistler constrained by impossible mother, leaving that place

indicators.note: constrained by means held inside, so the official goes within the scrambled letters
an impossible person is wild or unmanageable, signalling the word's letters are jumbled

parts.note: a referee blows a whistle, so is a whistler

explanation.surface: A child escapes a home where an unbearable mother hemmed in the painter Whistler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistler' tempts as the American painter but is the official who blows a whistle; 'impossible' scrambles the mother, which 'constrained by' wraps round him.
explanation.definitionFit: The old adverb means from there, describing departure out of the place just mentioned.

clue.text: Planet going around like the sun, day approaching fast

indicators.note: going around means encircling, so the planet's name wraps the other pieces

parts.note: Mars is the red planet
to dig something is slang for liking it
Ra was the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A planet orbiting the sun as a day draws on rapidly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' is the Lenten fast, not speed; 'like the sun' is two pieces, not a comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrove Tuesday is the carnival day just before the Lent fast begins on Ash Wednesday.

clue.text: Star in girl here, you bet!

indicators.note: in places the star inside the word for girl

parts.note: a lass is a girl
Vega is the brightest star in Lyra

explanation.surface: A girl starring in a show; here's a sure thing, you bet!
explanation.walkthrough: 'you bet!' looks like an exclamation of agreement, but read literally it says gambling happens here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nevada city is the world's gambling capital, the place to wager.

clue.text: Prison bog aligned with one of 24's characters, initially lacking

indicators.note: aligned with puts the bog word in line right after the shortened name
initially lacking means losing the first letter of the name

parts.note: Abel is one of the title pair in Archer's novel Kane and Abel
a marsh is a bog

explanation.surface: A jail in a swamp alongside a character from a novel, minus his initial.
explanation.walkthrough: Belmarsh is a high-security prison in south-east London, where Jeffrey Archer was briefly held after his perjury conviction in 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: Belmarsh is a category A jail in Thamesmead, London.

clue.text: Bird — tailless bird in daydream

indicators.note: in puts the docked bird inside the word for daydream

parts.note: to moon is to daydream or mope idly

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a rhea is a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: A bird, seen as a tailless bird lost in reverie.
explanation.definitionFit: The moorhen is a common water bird of ponds and rivers.

clue.text: Chuck contents of shoe, for the boot

parts.note: to chuck is to throw or heave

indicators.note: the contents of a word are its inner letters, leaving out the first and last

explanation.surface: Tipping out what's inside a shoe to make room for the boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the boot' means dismissal, not footwear, despite the shoe beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the boot and getting the heave-ho both mean being thrown out or sacked.

clue.text: Lib-Dem and Labour leaders arrested

parts.note: Nick Clegg led the Liberal Democrats in 2014
Ed Miliband led the Labour Party in 2014; 'leaders' covers both first names

explanation.surface: The heads of two British parties hauled off by police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' tempts one to take first letters, but it wants the leaders' first names: Nick Clegg and Ed Miliband, who led the Liberal Democrats and Labour in 2014.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicked is British slang for taken in by police.

clue.text: Drink, one in tune with Italy

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the word for tune

parts.note: a chant is a simple song or tune
I is the Roman numeral one
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A wine drunk while singing along with Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The red wine of Tuscany is a well-known Italian drink.

clue.text: One's bowled over by girl, a maiden in Madrid

indicators.note: bowled over means knocked head over heels, so the word is turned back to front

parts.note: the word read as written without its apostrophe
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone is smitten by a young woman, a Spanish maiden.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish title for a young unmarried woman is the equivalent of Miss.

clue.text: Backplate for armadillo, perhaps?

indicators.note: back here means the plate word is read in reverse

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer

explanation.surface: Wonders what the armour plating on an armadillo's back is for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backplate' looks like one word for armour, but splits as Back plus plate.
explanation.definitionFit: An armadillo is one example of a creature, hence the question mark.

clue.text: 24's going straight?

parts.note: a novel by the 24-across author, read as a phrase for travelling directly; and going straight also hints at an ex-convict reforming

explanation.surface: Asks whether the jailed author has reformed.
explanation.walkthrough: Going straight means both travelling in a direct line and giving up crime; Archer, jailed for perjury, wrote a novel whose title means the former.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeffrey Archer's 1991 novel has a title meaning by the most direct route.

clue.text: See 3
Author who's more devious?

definitions.meaning: Jeffrey ..., novelist of Kane and Abel
arch means sly or roguish, and this word is its comparative, read as describing a person

explanation.surface: Asks which writer is the craftier one.
explanation.walkthrough: Arch means cunning, so the comparative means more cunning; the jab at the perjurer novelist is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of Jeffrey Archer doubles as the comparative of arch, meaning sly.

clue.text: Straightening muscle enters ox with a bit jiggling

indicators.note: jiggling means shaken about, so the letters of the two words are shuffled

explanation.surface: An ox with a bit in its mouth enters, flexing its muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link; 'a bit jiggling' signals the anagram of ENTERS and OX.
explanation.definitionFit: An extensor is a muscle that extends or straightens a limb, the opposite of a flexor.

clue.text: It is so amazing making egg noodles for starters

indicators.note: starters are first courses, so the opening letters of the words are taken

explanation.surface: Praise for egg noodles served as a first course.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrew word said at the end of a prayer means so be it, or truly.

clue.text: Wet and naked, display rear in defiance and something on one's finger

parts.note: to show is to display

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its last letter

parts.note: a ring is worn on a finger

explanation.surface: A naked rebel shows his backside defiantly, wearing only a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone under the shower is both wet and unclothed.
